meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: выход всегда есть = there's always a way out

examples.text: Как говорит наш губернатор, выход всегда есть.
examples.trans: As our governor says, there's always a way out.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

examples.text: Каждый партнёр получил равную долю прибыли.
examples.trans: Each partner received an equal share of the profit.

examples.text: Отдай мне хотя бы мою долю.
examples.trans: Give me at least my share.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

жениться.gloss: to marry (of a man), to get married

meanings.en: to marry (на + prepositional, of a man); to get married

examples.text: А Даня на Нине женится! И будем жить дружно и фондю есть.
examples.trans: And Danya will marry Nina! And we will live together in harmony and eat fondue.

meanings.note: Как вы знаете = as you know.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?
All right, here you go. There, look.
I love our town very much.
You're in love with another man's wife!

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

начаться.gloss: to begin, to start, to break out

meanings.en: to begin, to start, to break out (intransitive)

examples.trans: The film started at seven sharp.

examples.text: Там начался пожар! Везде пожарные машины и полиция!
examples.trans: A fire started there! Fire engines and police are everywhere!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!
examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone about this, okay?
But legally you are nobody to her.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.en: to be offended, to take offence

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

examples.text: Я очень надеюсь, что вы не обидитесь.
examples.trans: I really hope you won't be offended.

examples.text: Я не поняла, ты сейчас на меня обиделся?
examples.trans: I didn't get it, are you offended at me now?

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.en: to answer, to reply, to pick up the phone

examples.text: Я вам звоню, а вы не отвечаете!
examples.trans: I call you, and you don't answer!

examples.text: Почему ты не отвечаешь на мои вопросы?
examples.trans: Why aren't you answering my questions?

examples.text: Всегда мечтала познакомиться с друзьями моего парня.
examples.trans: I've always dreamed of meeting my boyfriend's friends.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал. В Москву звал замуж!
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once. He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

поступить.gloss: to enter, to get into (a university); to act

examples.trans: Yulia needs to get into university.

examples.text: Вы плохо поступили, но хотя бы совесть есть.
examples.trans: You acted badly, but at least you have a conscience.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.
The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Сделать ставку = to place a bet.

examples.text: Там наливают бесплатно, если сделать ставку.
examples.trans: They pour for free if you place a bet.
The bets are placed, no more bets.

examples.text: Славик, смотри сюда. Меняю свой новый айфон на твой старый телефон.
examples.trans: Slavik, look here. I'll swap my new iPhone for your old phone.

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Also a mobile phone. International compound from Greek 'tele' (far) + 'phone' (voice, sound).

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

examples.text: Кстати, формально ты ведь выиграл пари.
examples.trans: By the way, technically you did win the bet.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Informal. Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.
But legally you're nothing to her.

examples.text: Чисто юридически ты ей не изменил.
examples.trans: Strictly legally speaking, you didn't cheat on her.

examples.text: А я тогда завтра известным юристом стану!
examples.trans: And then tomorrow I'll become a famous lawyer!

examples.text: Мне на заводе хороший юрист нужен.
examples.trans: I need a good lawyer at the factory.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
